entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Silvino Silvério Marques was a Portuguese colonial administrator and a general of the Portuguese Army. He was governor of Cape Verde from 1958 to 1962, and governor of Angola for two terms: from 1962 to 1966, and in 1974. He was administrator of the National Steel Industry from 1967 to 1970, interim director of Armed Engineers and 2nd Commander of the Military Region of Mozambique from 1971 to January 1973. In May 1974, he was installed by general António de Spínola as governor of Angola, but was removed from office after two months for not giving guarantees to follow instructions from the National Salvation Junta.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As governor of Angola from 1962 to 1966 and again in 1974, Silvino Silvério Marques played a role in the country's transition towards independence. His removal from office after two months in May 1974 had significant implications for the National Salvation Junta's control over the government.
